final_narrative:
The metabolomics profiling identified seven significantly differentially abundant metabolites with striking enrichment in steroidogenic pathways. The top candidate is **Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism** (KEGG map00150; FDR = 0.0, fold-enrichment = 1,429.7), confirmed by five of the seven input compounds — dihydrotestosterone (C03917), androstenedione (C00280), dehydroepiandrosterone (C01227), testosterone (C00535), and estradiol (C00951) — all with full co-occurrence plausibility (1.0). This pathway anchors a broader cluster of significant hits including **Metabolism of steroid hormones** (Reactome R-HSA-196071; FDR = 0.0) and **Classical pathway of steroidogenesis with glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid metabolism** (WP4523; FDR = 0.0), indicating a global perturbation of the steroid biosynthesis network.

The key driver compounds span the biosynthetic axis from adrenal precursors to potent end-products. **Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA, C01227)** occupies the most upstream position and feeds into **androstenedione (C00280)**, which in turn is a direct precursor of **testosterone (C00535)** — a two-hop KEGG reaction path (C01227 → C00280 → C00535). **Dihydrotestosterone (C03917)**, a downstream 5α-reduced androgen, was also elevated, consistent with heightened androgen receptor signalling capacity. **Estradiol (C00951)** anchors the estrogen arm of the same pathway, suggesting coordinated dysregulation of both sex-hormone branches.

The two remaining metabolites — **butanone (C02845)** and **sulindac (C01531)** — are pharmacologically contextual outliers; butanone is a ketone solvent with no established role in steroidogenesis, and sulindac is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug that may have been administered as part of the treatment regimen. Neither contributed to the steroid pathway enrichment signal.

The biological significance of this pattern depends on the treatment context. If the treatment involves anabolic agents, glucocorticoids, or endocrine-disrupting compounds, the coordinated elevation of DHEA through to dihydrotestosterone and estradiol would reflect activation of the steroidogenic cascade. In a disease model, such a signature could indicate aromatase overactivity (shunting androgens toward estrogens) or 5α-reductase overactivity (amplifying androgen potency), both of which are clinically relevant in hormone-sensitive cancers, polycystic ovary syndrome, or adrenal hyperplasia. Downstream consequences may include altered feedback at the hypothalamic–pituitary axis, shifted tissue androgen-to-estrogen ratios, and downstream impacts on lipid or glucose metabolism mediated by sex-steroid receptors.
